feedback: The confession follows the available distinction cleanly: Justin invented neutralization in a clipping whose actual correction concerned an owner's name. His motive also grows from the established omission of the settlement rather than an unrelated late secret. Taking poison at the preview is newly stated action, but it confirms the inferred mechanism rather than supplying a new decisive reason to choose him. The ending's strongest line is his realization that the surviving history now has to outlive his fabrication. Brie and Cary receive humane resolutions to their real financial faults without being artificially absolved of everything. The result feels earned, though the confession is concise enough that a little resistance before admission might heighten its emotional force.
